records.text: A Cyber-Rage Forgelord is one of the Burning Legion enemies Exarch Orelis sends the Aldor to kill in Netherstorm. It can enter a frenzy, cast Chaos Nova nearby, and enrage when badly hurt.
A Mo'arg Doomsmith is one of the Legion demons that Papa Wheeler says has moved into the Scrap Field east of Area 52. Its Doomsaw is a close-range attack.
A Gan'arg Engineer is one of the Legion demons that Papa Wheeler says has moved into the Scrap Field east of Area 52. It remains still while out of combat.
A Gan'arg Mekgineer, one of the enemies the Aldor targets at the Legion's Netherstorm forge bases. In combat it can steal a nearby weapon and drain life.
A gas-cloud creature called an Arcane Vortex, encountered across Netherstorm.

Kalynna left the Kirin Tor to pursue forbidden knowledge. She seeks two specific tomes in exchange for helping Alturus, and, if the tomes are supplied, promises to bind your essence to Arcanagos's to restore the dead dragon. She directs you to recover Arcanagos's essence for Alturus and warns of the danger if you fail.
Chief Engineer Lorthander is a named combatant who uses Arcane Unlocking, Slow, and Arcane Bolt, and may flee for aid when badly hurt.
Ever-Core the Punisher is an elemental sentinel that calls out intruders and threatens immediate neutralization, then uses Suppression in combat.
A Sunfury guardsman, this fighter marks foes with Mark of the Sunfury and may go into a frenzy in combat.
A Sunfury specialist at Manaforge B'naar, warp-engineers oversee the retrieval of warp-energy and its delivery through underground pipes. This engineer fights with a welding beam.
A Sunfury Bloodwarder guarding Manaforge B'naar, this fighter can mark foes with Mark of the Sunfury and go into a frenzy.

A Sunfury magister among Manaforge B'naar's defenses, it uses fire and bloodcrystal magic in battle and flees for aid when badly wounded. It also casts a red beam outside combat; its purpose is unclear.

The Arcane Annihilator is a mechanical combatant encountered in Netherstorm. It attacks with Suppression and Arcane Explosion, giving its name a literal edge: this machine is built to turn arcane power against its foes.

Sunfury Warp-Masters are specialists at Manaforge B'naar, where they oversee the retrieval of warp-energy and its delivery through underground pipes. Spymaster Thalodien identifies them as among the brains of the manaforge operation and a valuable target for disrupting Kael'thas's forces. In battle, a Warp-Master can use a welding beam.

Wrathbringers are Legion demons deployed at Forge Base: Oblivion and Forge Base: Gehenna. Aldor and Nether-Stalker Nauthis accounts describe the forge bases as important to the Legion's alliance with Kael'thas and its military buildup; Nauthis says Gehenna stages the Legion's army and houses many teleportation devices. Wrathbringers are among the forces sent there, and use a combat spell against their foes.
A Wrath Priestess is a Legion demon found at Forge Base: Gehenna.

Daughters of Destiny are demons serving the Burning Legion. Kaylaan's account links the Legion with Kael'thas's Sunfury army and says the demons enabled Kael'thas to use Tempest Keep's technology. They are among the forces targeted in Orelis's campaign; in combat, a Daughter of Destiny can unleash Chaos Nova.
A mana wraith that attacks nearby creatures with Devour Mana.
A warp aberration.
A hostile mana elemental known as a Mageslayer, found among the ruins of Wizard Row. It uses Spell Reflection and Blink in combat.
A hostile mana elemental known as a Mana Seeker, found in the ruins of Wizard Row. It uses Mana Burn in combat.
An unstable voidwraith that coalesces when it returns and releases an Unstable Rift when it dies.
A voidshrieker that absorbs holy, fire, nature, frost, shadow, and arcane energy from attacks. In combat it uses Shadow Bolt and Holy Smite.
The Disembodied Vindicator is a hostile Netherstorm creature.
The Disembodied Protector is a hostile creature found in Netherstorm. It can cast Holy Smite in combat.
The Zaxxis Raider is a Netherstorm creature that can cast Energy Flare at close range.
The Nether Drake is a Netherstorm creature that can cast Intangible Presence at nearby targets.
The Phase Hunter is a creature found across several Netherstorm areas. It casts Phase Slip in combat.
The Sundered Rumbler is a Netherstorm creature that can shatter into shards.
Sundered Thunderer is a Netherstorm creature whose death triggers a summon of Sundered Shards.
Warp Chasers are creatures found across several Netherstorm areas.
Farahlon Giant is a large Farahlon creature that summons a Farahlon Crumbler as it becomes injured.
Farahlon Breaker is a large Farahlon creature that summons a Farahlon Shardling as it becomes injured.
Krexcil is Netherstorm’s flight master; travelers can ask him about flying. When attacked, he summons an Enraged Gryphon and an Enraged Wyvern.

Ravandwyr is a Kirin Tor apprentice to Archmage Vargoth. Entrusted with his master's staff, he lost it while fleeing a Burning Legion force and remains ashamed of that failure. He seeks to restore the staff and free Vargoth, confined in the cursed Violet Tower. In Area 52, Ravandwyr also performs magic with his familiar, Sagan.

A Sunfury captain serving in Netherstorm, this humanoid fights for the Sunfury and uses Battle Shout in combat. The captain can also be heard announcing a frenzy, marking a moment of heightened aggression in battle.

Exarch Orelis is an Aldor leader in Area 52, investigating the manaforges operated by Kael'thas's forces with the Sha'tar's mission at stake. He accepts military action against the Sunfury to keep the Scryers gathering information, though he resents having to support them and distrusts the reliability of their defectors' reports. Orelis warns that warp energy from Tempest Keep's technology could endanger Outland, and favors measured attacks on the manaforges to learn more. He speaks fiercely in defense of a priestess of the Light.

Anchorite Karja is a Sha'tar emissary investigating Kael'thas's activities in Netherstorm. She argues that A'dal sent the Sha'tar to investigate, not launch a full-scale attack, and urges attention to the manaforges and their purpose. Fluent in Thalassian, she exchanges information with the Scryers and treats reports of the Burning Legion's alliance with Kael'thas as urgent, calling for word to be sent to Shattrath.

Spymaster Thalodien works with the Sha'tar to gather intelligence on Kael's manaforges. He studies their personnel and operations, then sends others after the specialists whose work sustains them; he is happy to spare himself the bloodshed. Once convinced that helping Kael would reunite the blood elves with their prince, he regretted leaving Falconwing Square when he learned what Kael intended. Thalodien remains openly hostile to Kael's forces and speaks with sardonic confidence about his own intelligence and his allies' successes.

At Area 52, Scryer magistrix Larynna studies the Sunfury's bloodgem use and its effect on mana addiction. She accepts striking Kael'thas's forces as a tactical necessity, though she takes no pleasure in killing her own kin as Thalodien does. She expects the bloodgem's side effects to be temporary and checks whether its effects were investigated.

Archmage Vargoth is a Kirin Tor mage who loves Dalaran as home and finds his retreat relaxing, though lonely. His struggle against Kael'thas's curse at the Violet Tower reveals practical resourcefulness: when the ward blocks his own scrying, he seeks an outside helper and a crystal focus. He respects Kael'thas's magical talent, recalls Sarannis from the attack on Kirin'Var, and distinguishes her possession of the ward's key from personally maintaining its magic.
Sagan is Ravandwyr's familiar, associated with a skunk transformation.

Custodian Dieworth is the undead Keeper of Kirin'Var, mourning the Kirin Tor destroyed by Kael'thas's forces and seeking vengeance on the Sunfury. Dieworth opposes Naberius, Vargoth's former apprentice, for enslaving the fallen spirits and denying them rest. Strong ties to the village also bind Dieworth: despite wanting to cease existing, the custodian admits not knowing how to let go.

Lieutenant-Sorcerer Morran is a Kirin Tor spirit at Kirin'Var Village whose identity endured after death. He works to protect the fallen Kirin Tor from mana creatures, directing efforts against Sunfury forces and adapting captured energy into a village ward. He is cautious about unfamiliar magic, but sees the perimeter as necessary.

Ar'kelos is the arcane golem Kael'thas placed at the bottom of the Violet Tower to guard it. Its assignment stands between Archmage Vargoth and his work inside the sealed tower; Vargoth identifies defeating Ar'kelos as the last step before he can resume his preparations there.
A Stormspire Nexus-Guard serves as an elite martial defender at the Stormspire, meeting nearby threats with sweeping and disabling strikes.
Eyonix is an innkeeper whose greeting is wry and warmly hospitable: he welcomes travelers swept in by the netherwinds, offers a place to rest at a modest fee, and lets them browse his goods.

Dealer Aljaan presents himself as a worldly tradesman with fair prices and hard-to-find supplies. His pitch turns coy when he mentions where the goods came from, suggesting a shrewd seller who prefers customers to focus on the bargain rather than ask about its origins.

Dealer Digriz sells ammunition and throwing weapons to travelers facing Netherstorm’s dangerous creatures. He stresses that ample ammunition may be vital to survival, then reassures customers that his prices are reasonable under the circumstances.

Dealer Zijaad sells common and exotic reagents for travelers who want potent spells in the dangerous Nether. He greets customers as powerful travelers and makes a confident sales pitch, promising that his wares will prove worthwhile.
Dealer Jadyan deals in exotic weapons and offers vendor and repair services to customers. His trade is aimed at travelers seeking unusual arms and practical equipment help.
Dealer Malij supplies enchanting materials to customers pursuing the craft.
Dealer Senzik deals in gems and Jewelcrafting supplies, serving customers who need stones and materials for their craft. His specialty is the gem trade and the supplies used by jewelcrafters.
Jazdalaad is a master jewelcrafting trainer who offers instruction and also has goods to browse. His greeting asks whether the visitor is interested in learning jewelcrafting.

Asarnan is a master enchanting trainer who offers instruction and also has goods to browse. His greeting challenges visitors to hone their skills before learning what he can teach, giving his training a more demanding tone.

These Netherstorm agents work shifts near neighbors with surplus machine parts and discuss gathering other agents to investigate. One wonders whether Papa Wheeler understands the danger posed by arcane annihilators. The remarks give this group a practical, wary view of the work around them.

Battle-Mage Dathric is a Kirin Tor spirit associated with quarters in Wizard's Row at Kirin'Var. His named sword is linked to his lingering presence: he regrets setting out without it, and the account of the blade suggests it may anchor his spirit. His summoned spirit follows a route and uses fire spells in combat.

Conjurer Luminrath is a Kirin Tor spirit associated with quarters in Wizard Row at Kirin'Var. His richly made cloak appears to connect him to this world: he looks for it, then reacts with relief when he finds it. The account suggests that returning the garment to his dresser may let his spirit rest.
Cohlien Frostweaver is a Kirin Tor gnome mage whose quarters lie in Wizard Row. His lucky hat matters enough that he calls it his and says he has been looking everywhere for it.
Abjurist Belmara is a Kirin Tor mage in Wizard Row who finds comfort in bedtime stories: after anticipating a good story, she says she is certain to rest well.
Dimensius the All-Devouring is a named adversary in Netherstorm. He describes himself as infinite, dismisses time as a mortal concern, and threatens that all will eventually be devoured.
An enormous void storm in Netherstorm.
An Unending Voidwraith, a demon found in Netherstorm.

Netherologist Coppernickels of B.O.O.M. studies the nether from a bridge away from town. His research and second-hand equipment trouble him; he wonders whether nearby blood elves think he is spying and suspects they may soon need to escape.

Rocket-Chief Fuselage commands B.O.O.M., the Braintrust of Orbital Operations and Mechanics, at Area 52. His dialogue makes the X-52 Nether-Rocket his personal project and dream: he calls it his masterpiece, recruits technicians to gather its parts and fuel, and urges Chief Engineer Trep and Doctor Vomisa to help advance the work. He speaks with exuberant confidence about the rocket and his ambitions for it.

Innkeeper Remi Dodoso runs an inn. Remi remarks that visitors from Shattrath arrived a few nights ago and have been arguing, worries that their dispute may drive away customers, and admits that their continued fighting is getting on Remi’s nerves.

Gant is a food-and-drink vendor serving customers in the Outland region represented by map 530, zone 3523. His recorded services identify him as a specialist in food and drink rather than a general supplier.

Dash is a trade supplies vendor serving customers in the Outland region represented by map 530, zone 3523. His recorded role is supplying trade goods, distinguishing him from the food-and-drink and general-supplies merchants nearby in the same region.

Kizzie is a general supplies vendor serving customers in the Outland region represented by map 530, zone 3523. Her recorded role covers general supplies, setting her apart from merchants with a more specialized stock focus.

Qiff is an engineering supplies vendor who also offers repairs. He serves customers in the Outland region represented by map 530, zone 3523; his engineering specialty and repair service distinguish his shop from the area's other suppliers.
Xyrol is a Master Engineering Trainer. Xyrol’s trainer greeting is a general invitation to demonstrate skill.

Bot-Specialist Alley is a B.O.O.M. specialist charged with recovering draenei machinery from the Ruins of Enkaat, while keeping the bots charged. Alley is concerned about Mk. V’s condition, calls the bot a source of pride, and hopes the work earns a promotion from Rocket-Chief Fuselage.
Maxx A. Million Mk. I is a mechanical bot and an ongoing project of Bot-Specialist Alley, who says she is always working on the Mk. I.
Grennik is a Netherstorm flight master who offers air travel. When attacked, he summons an Enraged Gryphon and an Enraged Wyvern.

Maxx A. Million Mk. II is one of Bot-Specialist Alley’s mechanical bots. Alley says it gained sentience briefly before its brain capacitor failed and it went insane; afterward, Alley skipped Mk. III and Mk. IV.

Maxx A. Million Mk. V is a charged, fully functional recovery machine sent into the Ruins of Enkaat to retrieve fragile draenei machinery. He boasts that his delicate wrist servos and pneumatic bump soakers let him handle the equipment carefully, though he expects ghosts to attack and asks for protection.

Spellbinder Maryana is identified as part of the garrison left behind by Kael'thas at Manaforge Coruu. The account of the speaker seeking the Sigil of Krasus says Kael'thas gave the artifact to her after taking it from them; that speaker hopes it can help break an enchantment.
Irradiated workers in Area 52 complain about singed eyebrows and recoil from a skunk, shouting for it to be kept away. Their recorded outbursts give these laborers a startled, irritable edge.
The Irradiated Manager is a humanoid in Netherstorm.

Boots is B.O.O.M.'s lead mixologist, a bartender who wants more than selling drinks. He is developing an explosive rocket-fuel brew from shaleskin oil and nether-ray venom to help launch the X-52, and cheerfully boasts that he can give a drink a kick. His bar greeting invites customers to order a drink.
Bill is identified as a B.O.O.M. Fire Marshal, placing him with the organization’s fire response.
Doc is identified with B.O.O.M.

Lead Sapper Blastfizzle is B.O.O.M.'s sap foreman, enthusiastic about Area 52's fissure operations and the Nether-Rocket. Blastfizzle dismisses radiation fears yet insists on nether helmets, blaming a former protégé's transformation into Dr. Boom on refusing one. Affection for Sparky Uberthruster coexists with determination to stop his attacks. Blastfizzle jokes fondly about exploding wagons and nearly destroying the town through excavation.

Captain Arathyn leads a ballista team outside Manaforge B'naar. Scryer investigators believe he carries a personnel roster valuable to their inquiry for the Sha'tar. His confident boast links the smell of nether in the morning with victory.
Warp-Raider Nesaad survived an attack by Nether-Stalker Khay’ji. Khay’ji seeks to end Nesaad’s operation at a small ethereal camp near the Heap.
A Zaxxis Stalker is a humanoid attacker that uses Backstab against nearby foes.
A Sunfury astromancer whose magic includes Fiery Intellect outside combat and Scorch in combat.

An image of Archmage Vargoth, a Kirin Tor mage imprisoned by Kael'thas's curse in the Violet Tower. Vargoth is Ravandwyr's master and hopes to break the enchantment that keeps him there. He seeks the return of Krasus's sigil, compendium and familiar Glacius, and describes Kael'thas as a former brother turned enemy. He is alarmed by Netherstorm's devastation and vows to oppose Kael'thas once free.

Papa Wheeler is a B.O.O.M. Mech Tech and a partner in the X-52 Nether-Rocket project. He treats the Heap as B.O.O.M.'s claim, seeks ethereal technology for the rocket, and asks for help against Legion forces; he calls himself a lover, not a fighter. He describes Mama Wheeler as his field partner.
A seasoned vindicator in Netherstorm.

Glacius is identified as a familiar held by Summoner Kanthin at Manaforge Duro. The quest's speaker calls Glacius their familiar and seeks to reclaim it; the claim that Kanthin tried to compel Glacius is presented as the speaker's suspicion.

A senior magister in Kael'thas's force sent against Kirin'Var, Kanthin is stationed at Manaforge Duro and holds the familiar Glacius as a trophy. The account of Glacius says he tried to compel it to serve him. In battle he uses Fireball, Frost Nova and Pyroblast, shifting movement with his mana and distance.
A Nether anomaly found in Netherstorm.

N. D. Meancamp runs B.O.O.M. Salvage and covets a fel reaver heart, planning to use it or sell it to interested clients. He offers a finder's fee and warns that nearby Zaxxis ethereals are dangerous, revealing a shrewd, profit-minded salvager.

Master Daellis Dawnstrike is a blood elf commander in Kael'thas's force, sent to Manaforge Duro to help control the area. Custodian Dieworth remembers him leading the attack on Kirin'Var from the front and killing many Kirin Tor mages, describing him as ferocious and merciless. Dieworth identifies him by his bow.

An archer serving in Prince Kael'thas's Sunfury forces, stationed at Sunfury Hold. Kirin'Var's resistance blames those forces for destroying the village and killing its people, and calls for vengeance against the garrison.

Chief Engineer Trep leads engineering for the X-52 Nether-Rocket at Area 52, though he says he applied for security and took the only opening left. He relies on Xyrol's oversight while trying to build the engines, and works with mana-wraith essence and etherlithium crystals despite admitting he is unsure what the power will do.

Mama Wheeler is a B.O.O.M. mech tech interested in Ethereal technology; she says she is glad to be among them so she can learn, and hopes to acquire some technology for herself. She asks visitors to gather small fel reaver parts as the Burning Legion moves into nearby claims, then reacts with alarm when told the Legion is targeting Area 52.
The Nether Beast is a creature that gains an aura after combat begins.

An Engineering Crewmember works on a ship that is not ready to launch. The crew is still calibrating fuse lengths and expects a long delay; this crewmember urges a would-be traveler to return to family, then entertains the idea that family might give them strength. The exchange presents a practical, patient voice focused on launch safety and preparation.

Doomclaw taunts goblins and orders workers to put their backs into their labor, threatening that they will taste the Claw if they do not work faster. He also boasts that he and his followers are coming for the goblins, marking him as an aggressive threat to them.

The Experimental Pilot works around a scientific project but says the science is beyond his understanding and describes flying as his ordinary job. His remarks about being ready to leave, not being the man his family expects, and not having brought them out here suggest discomfort with the situation and reluctance to involve them.

A Sunfury geologist at Manaforge B'naar, counted among the few specialists there alongside warp-masters and warp-engineers. Spymaster Thalodien identifies these specialists as important to Kael's manaforge operations; this geologist defends itself when attacked.
An off-duty engineer affiliated with B.O.O.M. Engineering, present in the Netherstorm area around Manaforge B'naar.

Arcanist Ardonis works on the energy pipeline at Manaforge Coruu, where shipments to Tempest Keep have more than doubled. He says the facility is understaffed and barely kept functional, and worries about another disaster like Ultris. When Commander Dawnforge orders reinforcements sent to Manaforge Duro, Ardonis protests the strain but answers to his commander.

Commander Dawnforge commands the Sunfury operation at Manaforge Coruu. After attacks on Manaforge Duro by mana creatures, he orders Ardonis to send reinforcements, warning that refusal will not be tolerated. He says security at Coruu has been increased after the attacks, and speaks with blunt authority to his subordinate.

Doctor Vomisa, Ph.T. is B.O.O.M.’s experimentalist at the Proving Grounds, where he builds and tests inventions. He created the Scrap Reaver X6000 and wants it tested for Area 52’s defense, watching and calibrating its servos during the trial. His joking feedback to its pilot gives him a playful, confident manner.
Lariel Sunrunner is based in Netherstorm.

Caledis Brightdawn conducts a Scryer operation against Kael's forces at Manaforge Coruu, using illusionary magic to disguise infiltrators. Caledis knows that real uniform details are needed to make the illusion convincing and warns that arcane golems can see through it. Working with Thalodien, Caledis first seeks intelligence from Dawnforge and Ardonis, then urges a rapid shutdown of the manaforge before the team is exposed.
Scrap Reaver X6000 is a mechanical combatant whose destruction leaves it in pieces.
An artifact-seeking demon whose combat repertoire includes Mana Burn.
A Felblade doomguard demon whose combat repertoire includes War Stomp.

Nether-Stalker Khay'ji is a Consortium agent working from Area 52. He says Nexus-Prince Haramad tasked him with acquiring an artifact from the Arklon Ruins, where the Legion has begun excavating old draenei ruins. Khay'ji also infiltrated the Zaxxis at the Heap and says he escaped after taking out their leader; he calls the Zaxxis traitors for breaking with the Consortium and dealing with the Sunfury. He admits he failed to stop Warp-Raider Nesaad, then recruits help to finish the job. His words show a direct, mission-focused agent who takes the Consortium's betrayal personally.

Severed Spirits are remnants of Kirin Tor mages left by the attack on Kirin'Var Village. They lost their former knowledge and wandered the ruins in blind anger; though initially restless rather than spiteful, they have grown increasingly aggressive. They are described as dangerous even to Custodian Dieworth.

Spellreaver Marathelle was a lieutenant of Kael'thas who took the heliotrope oculus to Sunfury Hold during the attack on the Violet Tower. The artifact was needed to unlock Krasus's Compendium. In combat, she quips about having picked the wrong day to quit mana tapping.

Apex is a crystal-bearing giant roaming the plains west of Manaforge Duro. Archmage Vargoth identifies one of its crystals as a useful focus for scrying the force behind the Violet Tower's ward, which Kael'thas's magic sustains.

Gahruj represents the Consortium at Midrealm Post, where he handles its business in Netherstorm. He is pursuing payment or recovery of surveying equipment from the blood elves after they failed to pay, and regards their conduct as damaging to business partnerships. He also asks for help with nearby Legion threats, showing concern for the safety of the post and its people. His comments present him as attentive to the consequences of Consortium dealings and appreciative of trustworthy assistance.

Zuben Elgenubi is a Consortium trader at the Stormspire, building a market for farahlite from the Netherstone. He sees higher-grade material from the Farahlon giants as a promising opportunity, even though obtaining it carries danger, and is eager to test a farahlite core. His twin brother Zuben Eschamali calls him a rising star while teasing his modesty; Zuben himself is focused on growing the trade.

Zuben Eschamali is a Consortium member at the Stormspire and Zuben Elgenubi's twin brother. He points out that Elgenubi is older by only a couple of minutes, then downplays the praise of Elgenubi as a rising star: Eschamali says he will never match his brother's stature as a trader. His remarks show familiarity with the Consortium's trading ambitions and a wry, self-deprecating view of his own prospects.

Wind Trader Marid is an ethereal dealer in exotic goods, building a new venture around nether-drake supplies. He hires a former employee as a subcontractor, but treats independent contractors with suspicion and expects them to be closely supervised. When that worker returns offering a deal, Marid proposes moving the discussion somewhere private, then reveals he intends to cut his losses rather than do business again.

Nexus-Prince Haramad appears at the Stormspire through an imaging device, a precaution because he says he has many enemies who would like him dead. He welcomes visitors with Consortium hospitality and seeks a legendary draenei crystal, believing it may grant god-like power. After the crystal is recovered, he entrusts it to a visitor for delivery to A'dal, admitting the achievement has inspired him to reconsider his own conduct.

Dealer Hazzin is a provisioner and an agent of Nexus-Prince Haramad at the Protectorate Watchpost on Manaforge Ultris. He supplies travelers preparing to approach the manaforge and warns them to resupply. He knows the triangulation mission and urges it forward, recognizing its importance to Haramad.

Tyri is Tyrygosa of the brood of Malygos, a blue dragon investigating the unfamiliar nether dragons with her companion Jorad Mace. She studies their eggs and seeks to understand the creatures and their rapid growth. Concerned that outsiders will exploit them for profit, she wants her flight to learn from them and intends to keep the scattered dragons from falling under a malevolent power.
Jorad Mace is Tyri’s companion on the Celestial Ridge, where they investigate the nether dragons. He is among those seeking to learn about the dragons and their eggs.

Wind Trader Tuluman is an ethereal weapon merchant at Tuluman’s Landing near Manaforge Ara. He wants the blood elf mining operation at Trelleum Mine disrupted and sees a chance for his side to take it over. He welcomes trade before dangerous ventures and thanks those who report what happens there.

Socrethar is a powerful eredar whom Aldor and Scryer forces seek to defeat. He mocks the Aldor army, orders Kaylaan to earn a place in the Burning Legion, and later threatens to kill the challengers himself. His dialogue presents him as contemptuous of the attackers and confident in his strength.
An image of Socrethar, a demon in Netherstorm.
A Sunfury arcanist serving Kael’s forces at Manaforge Coruu. Exarch Orelis identifies the regiment there as an important target, and the arcanists are among its deployed forces.
A Sunfury arch mage serving Kael’s forces in Netherstorm.
A Sunfury researcher serving Kael’s forces. Exarch Orelis describes researchers and arcanists as an important regiment deployed at Manaforge Coruu, where they are targets of the Aldor’s operation.

Culuthas is a dreadlord associated with the Burning Legion’s occupation of the Ruins of Farahlon. He claims the ata'mal crystal for himself and threatens to use its power against anyone who challenges him.

A Sunfury conjurer serving Kael’s army in Netherstorm. Magistrix Larynna describes Sunfury stragglers as targets of opportunity during the mana creature assault, while acknowledging the cost of attacking her own kin.

A Sunfury soldier serving in Kael's army, this centurion is one of the forces stationed in Netherstorm. Scryer agents target the centurions alongside other Sunfury troops to weaken that army, while the centurion's known combat behavior includes casting Spellbreaker at close range.

A demonic hound serving Culuthas, this creature is among the forces he summoned after taking control of the Burning Legion presence at Farahlon. Its combat abilities include a double breath and a heavy stomp; Nether-Stalker Nauthis asks adventurers to hunt these hounds and the Eyes of Culuthas around the ruins.
A dead doomguard found among the demons at Farahlon.

A concealed watcher who presents a projection so that they and a companion can observe the unusual nether dragonkin without revealing themselves. The figure studies the dragons and seeks an arrangement with adventurers to gather their essence for a client, while warning that Marid is a swindler. Their slipped reference to “K” hints at the client's identity, which they deliberately withhold; they say further questions will be answered later.

Veronia arranges windrider flights to Manaforge Coruu for an operation behind enemy lines, where agents are sent to meet two spies and gather information on Kael’s forces. She handles the journey and cautions travelers to bring what they need before the drop.
Dealer Dunar is a general provisioner whose welcome makes buying and selling sound like a friendly exchange. He calls the visitor “my friend” and warmly invites them to say what they would like.
Cragskaar is the patriarch of the Farahlon giants, with huge pieces of farahlite jutting from its back. Zuben Elgenubi seeks a farahlite core from this giant as a higher-quality sample.
B.O.O.M. Nether Technicians are present at several sites in Netherstorm. Their title identifies a technical role and organizational association.
Action Jaxon is one of Shauly’s associates at the Stormspire, alongside Audi the Needle. Shauly directs a visitor to find them there for information and to say that Shauly sent them.

Audi the Needle works with Action Jaxon and Shauly on a discreet eco-dome scheme. Under cover of hunting, she and Jaxon collect generator segments and hide them in raptor nests at Eco-Dome Farfield. Guarded about the “merchandise,” she seeks help recovering it and hopes to supply Area 52, interest the Cenarion Expedition and earn a profit.
A Sunfury soldier in Kael's army, armed as a bowman. Scryer Magistrix Larynna orders a strike against Sunfury forces during the mana-creature assault, including bowmen.
A Shaleskin beast appearing in several parts of Netherstorm; it casts Shaleskin while out of combat.

Pentatharon is a dreadlord involved in the Burning Legion's excavation of the old draenei Arklon Ruins. Nether-Stalker Khay'ji seeks a crystal artifact from him. Pentatharon uses Carrion Swarm in combat.
Sunfury Flamekeepers are combatants who use Torch and Judgement of the Flame. Their battle behavior includes erupting into a frenzy.

Karaaz is a Consortium quartermaster who advertises smuggled goods as a way around goblin taxation and naaru prohibition. Karaaz denies selling stolen goods while asking customers not to name their source, and offers items said to have fallen from a Nagrand pack mule. Blueprints, patterns and schematics are promoted as exceptionally easy to use.
A scrapped fel reaver with a mechanical heart that can begin beating softly.

Sunfury nethermancers channel energy to and from blood gems to stabilize the power flow at Manaforge Ara. Nether-Stalker Oazul targets them to disrupt operations he blames for destroying the surrounding land.

Drijya works with Gahruj to stop Burning Legion reinforcements through the warp-gate at Invasion Point: Destroyer. He recruits companions to protect him during sabotage, moves briskly between energy pylons and the heat manifold, and asks that Gahruj be told of the result. On success, Drijya gratefully acknowledges that he could not have managed without help.

Dr. Boom is the infamous former Area 52 protégé Sparky Uberthruster, according to Lead Sapper Blastfizzle, who says he stole sapping equipment and became a menace with his Boom Bots. He operates near Area 52; the bombs in Blastfizzle's request and Dr. Boom's own dynamite attack both make explosives central to the encounter.

A Gan'arg Warp-Tinker is one of the Legion-aligned demons targeted alongside Mo'arg Warp-Masters in the Aldor account of a dangerous alliance with Kael'thas's Sunfury army. These Netherstorm enemies use Mana Bombs and try to steal weapons at close range.

Mo'arg Warp-Masters are named with Gan'arg Warp-Tinkers as demons serving the dangerous alliance of the Burning Legion and Kael'thas's Sunfury army, as described by the Aldor. A Warp-Master attacks nearby foes with Slime Spray.
Nether Dragons are dragon creatures found in Netherstorm. This kind casts Intangible Presence on nearby targets.
Fleshfiends are combat creatures that cast a spell while fighting.

Nether-Stalker Oazul is a Consortium contact who condemns the blood elves’ manaforge operations. He says their nethermancers stabilize the energy flow, and directs attention to disrupting that work at Manaforge Ara.

Lee Sparks, called the Taskmaster, describes himself as a retired rogue. He says he trained Daniels, the Specialist, and served with him in the trenches; he believes Daniels is still active in Zangarmarsh.

Foreman Sundown was demoted from running the Trelleum Mine. He believes Kael'thas used the Quel'Thalas pilgrimage to Outland as a pretext to build his forces, and has tried to persuade his fellow blood elves to leave as the Burning Legion advances. When confronted, he insists he is no longer the enemy.

An Eye of Culuthas is one of the demons serving Culuthas in the Ruins of Farahlon, part of the infestation that the Stormspire's agents seek to clear. Eyes of Culuthas are hunted alongside Hounds of Culuthas.

Overseer Seylanna oversees Manaforge Coruu and holds its access crystal. Both Aldor and Scryer operations seek that crystal to use the control console and shut down the manaforge, putting her at the center of their rival efforts against the facility.
A demon identified as a warp-gate engineer, found in Netherstorm.
An apprentice associated with Kirin'Var in Netherstorm. It throws a hammer at ranged opponents.

Rhonsus is the ghost of Kirin’Var Village’s master blacksmith. Apprentice Andrethan’s account describes him as once expected to receive a journeyman project; the quest later calls for confronting Rhonsus after the town’s dead have become hostile. He returns under a Shroud of Death.
Spectral Bovine is a ghostly bovine found among the fields near Kirin’Var Village. These creatures return under a Shroud of Death.

Bessy is Thadell’s prize cow, a distinct animal recognized by her cowbell. She can be wary when approached and moos calmly or angrily when attacked. Her story involves being found in the fields and escorted toward her owner; she does not speak words.

Overseer Theredis is identified as holding the access crystal for Manaforge B’naar. Aldor and Scryer accounts both direct an operative to obtain it so the manaforge can be shut down safely; the accounts differ in who receives the report. Theredis is described as an overseer.

Overseer Athanel holds the access crystal for Manaforge Duro, which is needed to shut the unstable manaforge down safely. Aldor and Scryer accounts agree on the crystal’s purpose but present different reasons for urgency and different reporting contacts.
A Sunfury Protector is a martial guard serving Sunfury forces in Netherstorm. It attacks when directed and fights after being summoned.
A Protectorate vanguard, a humanoid found in Netherstorm.

Commander Ameer is an ethereal of the Protectorate, impatient with outsiders who mistake all ethereal factions for one. Addressing them as “fleshlings,” Ameer confidently offers help against void creatures and the Ethereum. The commander orders attacks against potential threats while seeking to decode prisoner records and free allies with minimal exposure to hostile action. Protecting lives motivates that rescue work.

Researcher Navuud is the Protectorate Watch Post's chief researcher. Concerned about toxic sludge and void waste around Ultris, Navuud warns that they can congeal into a void horror if left unchecked. Navuud prescribes electro-shock to break the slimes into globules for disposal and reacts with astonished enthusiasm to a rare sample of void horror ooze.

Flesh Handler Viridius is an ethereal flesh handler, a specialist in dealing with flesh and beings of flesh. Viridius asks for help locating and freeing Captain Tyralius, whose distress signal may mean he is imprisoned by the Ethereum.
A subservient flesh beast found at the Ethereum Staging Grounds in Netherstorm.

An Ethereum assassin stationed at the Staging Grounds, where the Ethereum are preparing for a possible assault on Ultris. Commander Ameer identifies assassins among the facility's soldiers and orders them taken out.

An Ethereum shocktrooper stationed at the Staging Grounds, where the Ethereum are preparing for a possible assault on Ultris. Commander Ameer identifies shocktroopers among the facility's soldiers and orders them taken out.

Nexus-King Salhadaar is protected by force fields sustained by three conduits at the Ethereum Staging Grounds. Commander Ameer directs their destruction to expose Salhadaar, who threatens intruders with oblivion and declares himself a god.

An Ethereum Researcher serving in the Ethereum force at the staging grounds south of the area where Commander Ameer directs an assault against Ultris. Researchers there are among the targets in Ameer's orders; this one fights with the force and casts a spell in combat.
An Ethereum Archon stationed with the Ethereum force at the staging grounds. It responds to combat with spells.
An Ethereum Overlord among the Ethereum force at the staging grounds. It casts a spell when attacked.

Apprentice Andrethan is a smith in Kirin'Var Village, working toward journeyman standing. He misplaced the hammer he brought to shoe Farmer Natin's horses and fears the other apprentices may copy his design. After learning that his master, Rhonsus, has become dangerous, Andrethan reluctantly considers killing him, then vows to honor Rhonsus by serving the town as its smith.

Thadell is an elderly herdsman in Kirin'Var Village whose cow Bessy went missing after an attack. He lends out her cowbell to help find her and is deeply attached to her, greeting her with relief and thanking the person who brings her home.

Zephyrion is an excavator at the Stormspire who wants to investigate the Ruins of Farahlon, but demonic occupation has kept his team from starting work. He asks for preliminary surveying there and, once the markers are placed, says he can take his team to explore what the ruins hold.

Nether-Stalker Nauthis is a Stormspire operative focused on countering the Burning Legion around Farahlon. With demons blocking Zephyrion's excavation, Nauthis directs efforts against Culuthas's forces and pursues sabotage of the Legion's inactive fel reavers and a reduction of its troops at Forge Base: Gehenna.
A fixed surveying marker in the Ruins of Farahlon, one of three placed near draenei banners for Zephyrion’s excavation survey.
An Ethereum nexus-stalker summoned to guard a conduit. It calls out to protect the conduit and stop intruders, reflecting the Ethereum’s hostile activity in Netherstorm.
A fixed surveying marker in the Ruins of Farahlon, one of three placed near draenei banners for Zephyrion’s excavation survey.
A fixed surveying marker in the Ruins of Farahlon, one of three placed near draenei banners for Zephyrion’s excavation survey.

The Image of Commander Ameer represents the Protectorate and calls the traveler “fleshling”, warning of dangerous work. When shown recovered Ethereum evidence, it describes plans to become void by bonding energy with nexus-stalkers and urges destruction of the captive creatures the Ethereum hope to command.

Naberius is Archmage Vargoth's apprentice, whose pursuit of necromancy brought destruction to Kirin'Var. He enslaves the spirits of fallen Kirin Tor, denying them rest, and fights with frost magic and Chains of Naberius.
A large bruiser found in Area 52. Its name distinguishes it from the regular Area 52 Bruisers, sharing their humanoid bruiser identity in a larger form.
A regular Area 52 Bruiser, found around the outpost. It is the common-sized counterpart to the larger Area 52 Big Bruisers.
A skeletal horse found near Kirin'Var Village. When it returns, it casts Shroud of Death.
An elemental creature found in the Sundered Shard region, bearing the same name as the place.
A seeping sludge that attempts to split in two and breaks down into globules. On respawn, it casts Darkstalker Birth.
A tormented Kirin Tor undead in Netherstorm that attacks when engaged.
Harpax is a flight master in Netherstorm. His flight menu asks where you would like to fly; when attacked, he summons an enraged gryphon and then an enraged wyvern.
A Netherstorm warp monstrosity that unleashes a warp storm when engaged and casts arcane bolts during combat.

Marid's summoned image reflects his hard-nosed trading outlook: he sorts people into competitors, customers, and employees, and distrusts independent contractors. He seeks nether dragon essence for a client, nearly revealing the client's name as K, and says a power cell will help his operation earn more profit.
An Ethereum prisoner in Netherstorm.

Agent Araxes is a Protectorate agent stationed outside Access Shaft Zeon. Ordered to remain until backup arrives, he gives out an igniter to destroy the withered corpses and reports that Arconus caused the slaughter. A transponder exchange reveals that he and Ya-six were separated in the firefight, and Araxes requests backup.

Agent Ya-six is a Protectorate agent trapped and badly injured in the Ultris mine after a firefight separated him from Araxes. Their mission is to find and terminate Arconus, whom Ya-six says had been feeding on creatures in the area. He asks for help and offers to provide a guardian reflection.

This image of Commander Ameer contacts Araxes through a transponder during a communications exchange disrupted by warp storms. Ameer requests a status report, says backup is on the way, and orders Araxes to hold position.

Arconus the Insatiable is a void lord tracked to the Ultris mine by Protectorate agents. Ya-six says Arconus had been feeding on the energies of creatures in the area, making him the target of the agents' mission.

Withered corpses are husks left after Arconus drains creatures in the Ultris mine. Araxes warns that flesh beasts inside can pounce on anyone who approaches. Protectorate Igniters can destroy the corpses.

Image of Agent Ya-six is a Protectorate agent whose distress message places him pinned down in the mines. He says flesh beasts block his route back and asks Araxes to send help; he had marked his way with tracers but cannot follow them out.
A Craghide Basilisk of the Eco-Domes, it can lie still as if dead before suddenly charging forward.
A Talbuk Doe of the Eco-Domes, it can call for a nearby male and may weaken.
A Shimmerwing Moth found in the Eco-Domes, it uses a spell while in combat.
The Ethereum Relay can cast Shadowform and Ethereum Relay.
A Scythetooth Raptor of Eco-Dome Farfield, it is a threat to the dome's generator according to technician Tashar. It attacks with a spell when provoked.
A Ripfang Lynx found in the Eco-Domes, it uses Swipe while in combat.
A Swiftwing Shredder is a beast that attacks with Lightning Breath.

Overseer Azarad is a sin'dorei overseer associated with Manaforge Ara, where the access crystal is said to be in his possession. Aldor and Scryer mission briefings describe the forge as a vital part of Kael's operation and warn that reaching the crystal means heavy opposition. Those accounts belong to the quest-givers, not Azarad.

Captain Zovax is an Ethereum captain at the faction's staging grounds and training facility. Commander Ameer describes the Ethereum as preparing for a possible assault on Ultris and orders Zovax's defeat as part of breaking through their defenses; this is Ameer's assessment, not Zovax's own account.
An Ethereum Energy Cell is a mechanical energy cell found among the Ethereum at their staging grounds.

A Protectorate soldier captured after his platoon’s reconnaissance mission was ambushed by attackers he believes were Ethereum. He says Tyralius was the only one spared and thinks he was taken to a prison cell. After escaping, he needs an escort back to the Protectorate Watch Post and thanks his rescuer before Commander Ameer.
An Ethereum Target in Netherstorm.
Warden Icoshock is a humanoid warden who uses Shadowtouched and Shadowsurge in combat.

Netherock is described by Rocket-Chief Fuselage as the king of the local mountain giants. Fuselage says Netherock has terrorized the Crumbling Wastes and disrupted operations along the island’s south ledge, including work on the X-52 Nether-Rocket.

A Farahlon Lasher is a widespread plant creature in the Netherstorm region, found across several local areas. When attacked, it can enter a frenzy and use Flanking Growth. Its recorded behavior is that of a dangerous living plant rather than a service-bearing resident.
Talbuk Sires are beasts found across several areas of Netherstorm.
Void Waste is an elemental creature found in Netherstorm. It breaks down into globules, and in combat it can use Toxic Burst.
A Congealed Void Horror is a void creature found in Netherstorm.

Kaylaan is a combatant serving under Orelis at Tuluman’s Landing. He says ten of his group entered Manaforge Ara and the others fell to the Legion. Though committed to the naaru, he grows disillusioned with orders that send them against the naaru’s enemies; he calls on the Light to protect his allies and speaks of failure when overwhelmed.

Captain Tyralius led a platoon south toward the Ethereum Staging Grounds, then went missing. Protectorate instruments registered what Viridius thought might be a distress signal, and the search report says Ethereum could be holding Tyralius in a prison. In his rescue response, he thanks the person who freed him and says Ameer will hear of the act.

Forgemaster Morug is at Forge Base: Oblivion. Both Aldor and Scryer mission briefings identify him as possessing the first half of Socrethar’s teleportation stone, needed to reach Socrethar’s Seat. In combat, he uses Chainsaw Blade and Slime Spray.

Silroth is a demon at Forge Base: Gehenna and holds the second half of Socrethar’s teleportation stone, sought by both Aldor and Scryer agents to reach Socrethar’s Seat. In combat, he uses Chemical Flames and Felforge Flames.

Overmaster Grindgarr is a demon opposed by a disillusioned former foreman, who seeks Grindgarr’s death after rejecting the pilgrimage that brought blood elves to Outland. The foreman wants Wind Trader Tuluman told that their enmity is over.
A Netherstorm Moarg Work Target in Netherstorm.

Mehrdad tends the Consortium’s eco-dome interests and worries about damaged shield generators. Consortium policy puts its equipment ahead of destructive crocolisks. Mehrdad sees profit in selling ivory bells to the Cenarion Expedition, despite their plain appearance, and warns visitors to be wary of Shauly’s overly familiar manner.

Ghabar is the Stormspire's head Eco-Dome engineer, cautious about unexplained generator failures and unwilling to accept ordinary creature damage as their cause. Ghabar values Mehrdad's eye for detail and trusts Tashar to test a portable repair kit for Consortium domes. Suspected sabotage worries Ghabar, who considers securing the Stormspire against theft of its technology.
Tyralius is an Ethereum prisoner.
An Ethereum gladiator that casts a spell in combat.
A Netherstorm arena-event controller identified with arena events.

Aurine Moonblaze is a Cenarion Expedition researcher studying how the ethereal domes affect plants and animals. Her work on accelerated growth has exposed risks such as extreme aggression and shortened lifespans, yet she remains determined to persuade the Consortium to share the technology, hoping controlled use could restore ruined lands.
Protectorate nether drake that carries riders toward Ultris for Professor Dabiri's operation against the Void Conduit, bringing them within range to deploy the phase disruptor.

Professor Dabiri is an Ethereal at the Protectorate Watch Post, focused on the danger Dimensius poses. He describes Dimensius as a longtime enemy of the Ethereals and concentrates on stopping him despite Ameer's concern about the Ethereum. Dabiri directs efforts to destroy Dimensius's void conduit and supplies a phase disruptor for the assault.

Tashar is a Consortium technician stationed at Eco-Dome Farfield, where he tests a portable generator repair kit designed by Ghabar. He is wary of the risks to a failing dome and of wildlife interfering with the test, drawing on years of work in strange environments. He also identifies missing generator parts across several sites as theft.

Magister Theledorn is a Sunfury magister stationed at Manaforge Ara who has made contact with the Scryers and offers information. When addressed, he questions whether the visitor was sent by the Scryers and observes that they do not look like one.

Shauly Pore is an Area 52 agent posing as a simple furrier at Midrealm Post while appraising the ethereals’ eco-dome technology. She recruits non-goblin agents to gather lynx pelts as cover, then directs them to her associates at the Stormspire; her wink suggests she enjoys maintaining the disguise.
A fallen vindicator: an elite humanoid combatant in Netherstorm.
An Ironspine Forgelord in Netherstorm, equipped with several combat spells.
Hatecryer is a demon that casts a spell in combat.
Tyrantus is a named beast.
Nuramoc is a named beast.
A Severed Defender is a Kirin Tor defender found in the Violet Hold. On returning, it casts Shroud of Death, marking it as an undead threat within the prison.
Dealer Rashaad is an exotic-creature merchant in Area 52, Netherstorm. He offers goods for browsing, and his stock centers on exotic creatures.
Dealer Najeeb sells spare parts and offers his goods for browsing.
A Protectorate Defender serves as a combatant for the Protectorate. In battle, it uses Glaive and Hamstring.

Captain Saeed leads the Protectorate's Avengers against Dimensius, a foe his people have hunted for a thousand years. He identifies with K'aresh and the Protectorate, and his soldiers wait for his command to attack.
Dealer Sadaqat deals in potent potables and offers his goods for browsing.
The Disembodied Exarch is an undead entity.
A Tormented Citizen bears the Kirin Tor label and is a combatant. It casts spells during combat and when attacked.
The Farahlon Crumbler is a creature in Netherstorm.
A Sunfury Blood Knight is a combatant in Netherstorm. It casts a spell during combat.
Professor Dabiri is a named professor in Netherstorm.
A Legion Fel Cannon is a combat machine found across several parts of Netherstorm.
Crash Bigbomb is identified with B.O.O.M. Sap Operations and appears in Outland.

Kablamm Farflinger is a goblin transportation engineer in Area 52. He says he and his brother Zap built a Dimensional Imploder there, reflecting his faith in Goblin Engineering’s instant transportation. He jokes that goblin engineers laugh at danger.
Nandirx is a banker in Outland who offers access to a personal bank for storing and retrieving belongings.
Karzo is a banker in Outland who offers access to a personal bank for storing and retrieving belongings.
Zixxy is a banker in Netherstorm who offers access to a personal bank.
Chubis is a B.O.O.M. Jr. mech tech in Area 52.
The Protectorate Regenerator is a humanoid figure found in two Netherstorm areas; its title combines the Protectorate name with a regenerative role.
A humanoid Protectorate Avenger is found in the Netherstorm Eco-Domes; in combat, it casts Glaive.
A demonic Terrorguard Protector is found at sites in Netherstorm; in combat it casts spells.
The Air Force Alarm Bot is a mechanical unit associated with Area 52, where multiple bots are present.
A mechanical Death Machine stationed in Area 52.

records.text: A goblin-built Air Force guard post at Area 52’s zeppelin site, part of the outpost’s defenses.

npcs.name: Air Force Trip Wire - Rooftop (Goblin - Area 52)

records.text: A rooftop trip wire in Area 52’s goblin Air Force defenses, positioned to detect intruders.
An ethereal Air Force guard post stationed in the Stormspire, serving its local defenses.

npcs.name: Air Force Trip Wire - Rooftop (Ethereal - Stormspire)

records.text: A rooftop trip wire in the Stormspire’s ethereal Air Force defenses, positioned to detect intruders.
An alarm bot stationed in the Stormspire, part of the ethereal Air Force’s defenses.
Nadja is a humanoid found in Netherstorm.
Soren is a humanoid found in Netherstorm.
This inactive fel reaver is a dormant machine. Its engine begins to rumble and sputter when supplied with incorrect fuel, and the reaver itself announces an engine malfunction.

Zarevhi is a Consortium ethereal and a renowned transmuter who offers specialized transmutation instruction. He asks aspiring transmuters to prove their skill with Primal Might and describes the knowledge he shares as mastery of conjuring matter through alchemy. He presents himself as famous across many worlds and, after arranging a sale of Primal Might, says he is going to meet a buyer.

Sab'aoth runs a reagent and poison supply business at Cosmowrench. He says he once amused himself by accepting challenges, but has tired of easy victories; he is now building his reagent trade and writing a book about his experiences in Twilight's Hammer. Warp chaser blood is one of his major sellers, and he normally relies on his imp, Zeppit, to gather it.
Zeppit is Sab'aoth's imp and can handle warp chaser blood safely, making him useful to the reagent seller. Sab'aoth says the imp's attention tends to wander and that he has a nasty mouth.
Kerpow Blastwrench is a weapon merchant in Netherstorm who sells goods and offers repairs.
A Cosmowrench bruiser, a humanoid found in Netherstorm.
Ethereum Nullifier is an Ethereum combatant found in Netherstorm. It casts a spell when it draws aggro.

Protectorate Advisor Rahim is a named representative of the Protectorate in Netherstorm. He says he acts at Nexus-Prince Haramad’s behest and reports that strange things are afoot at the Stormspire, tying his words to Haramad’s concerns there.
Ethereum Jailor is an Ethereum combatant encountered in Netherstorm. It casts spells while fighting and when drawing aggro.
Liza Cutlerflix is a named stable master in Netherstorm. Her greeting offers help with stabling pets and recovering lost companions.

The Netherstorm Flame Warden welcomes visitors to honor the local festival fire and urges them to honor Alliance flames while desecrating Horde ones. Its words frame the observance in openly Alliance-partisan terms.

The Netherstorm Flame Keeper is a Horde festival figure whose greeting invites visitors to honor fires in Horde settlements. He also urges desecrating Alliance fires, making his festival guidance explicitly partisan.
Blazzle is identified with blacksmithing supplies and offers a goods-browsing service, along with repairs. This establishes a practical trade role centered on materials and equipment work.
Kezzik the Striker is presented as a vendor, with his epithet providing a personal distinction beyond that practical role.
Big Zokk Torquewrench is an arena vendor.
Kezzik the Striker is identified as a veteran arena vendor, marking experience in the arena trade.
Leeni "Smiley" Smalls is an apprentice arena vendor. The title places this character at an apprentice rank in the arena trade.
Leeni “Smiley” Smalls is labeled an Apprentice Arena Vendor. She is in Netherstorm.
Kezzik the Striker is a Veteran Arena Vendor in Netherstorm. He offers goods to browse.
Big Zokk Torquewrench is labeled an Arena Vendor. He is in Netherstorm.
Big Zokk Torquewrench is an Arena Vendor in Netherstorm. He offers goods to browse.
Kezzik the Striker is a Veteran Arena Vendor in Netherstorm. He offers goods to browse.
Leeni “Smiley” Smalls is an Apprentice Arena Vendor in Netherstorm. She offers goods to browse.
Grex Brainboiler is an Exceptional Arena Weaponry vendor. His service menu offers access to his goods.

place_records.text: You are in Netherstorm, a region of Outland held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Its main settlements, Area 52, Cosmowrench and The Stormspire, answer to no side. Sunfury blood elves work the manaforges, while Zaxxis raiders, mana wraiths and warp chasers roam the land, and Burning Legion demons come through warp-gates.

You are in Area 52, a base in Netherstorm that neither side holds. Rocket-Chief Fuselage and the engineers of B.O.O.M. are building the X-52 Nether-Rocket here, while Exarch Orelis of the Aldor and Anchorite Karja of the Sha'tar investigate Kael'thas's manaforges. It has an inn and a bank.
You are in the Crumbling Waste, an area of Netherstorm. Phase hunters, nether beasts, nether rays and mana snappers roam its ground.

You are in Manaforge Ara, a Sunfury manaforge in Netherstorm. Sunfury nethermancers and Burning Legion servants are found inside it, and Magister Theledorn there offers information to the Scryers. Foreman Sundown, demoted from the Trelleum Mine, is trying to persuade his fellow blood elves to leave.

You are in Arklon Ruins, a hotbed of Burning Legion activity in Netherstorm. Artifact seekers and felblade doomguards are among its dangers, and Ekkorash, the Legion's leader in the ruins, holds Archmage Vargoth's staff.

You are in Cosmowrench, a settlement in Netherstorm that neither side holds. Sab'aoth runs a reagent and poison supply business here, Kerpow Blastwrench sells weapons, and Harpax keeps the flight master's post.

You are in the Ruins of Enkaat, a draenei ruin in Netherstorm where B.O.O.M. is recovering draenei machinery. Bot-Specialist Alley keeps her charged machines at work, Maxx A. Million Mk. V among them, while disembodied vindicators and protectors haunt the ruins.

You are in Manaforge B'naar, a Sunfury manaforge in Netherstorm. Sunfury bloodwarders, warp-engineers and magisters are the threat there, and the Aldor and the Scryers both take an interest in what the manaforge is doing.
You are in the Scrap Field, a fel reaver scrap field in Netherstorm where the Burning Legion is nearby. Gan'arg engineers, Mo'arg doomsmiths and doomclaws are the dangers there.

You are in the Vortex Fields, a part of Netherstorm where warp chasers, mana snappers and nether beasts roam, and Sunfury bowmen are among the dangers. Zeppit, an imp belonging to the reagent seller Sab'aoth, can handle warp chaser blood safely.

You are in The Heap, a salvage ground in Netherstorm that B.O.O.M. claims as its own. N. D. Meancamp runs B.O.O.M. Salvage here and offers finder's fees for fel reaver parts. Zaxxis raiders and stalkers are the dangers.

You are in Manaforge Coruu, a Sunfury manaforge in Netherstorm. Caledis Brightdawn runs a Scryer operation here, disguising infiltrators with illusion magic, and arcane golems patrol the manaforge. Sunfury arcanists and guardsmen are the dangers.
You are in the Tempest Rift, a part of Netherstorm where warp chasers and nether beasts roam, and swiftwing shredders are also seen.

You are in Manaforge Duro, a manaforge in Netherstorm where blood elves are having trouble with an infestation of mana creatures. Sunfury conjurers, bowmen and centurions are found here, with nether beasts and nether anomalies nearby.

You are in Voidwind Plateau, a Netherstorm plateau that neither side holds. Protectorate defenders and avengers can be found here, and ethereum nullifiers, jailors and shocktroopers, craghide basilisks and unending voidwraiths make it dangerous.

You are in Manaforge Ultris, a manaforge in Netherstorm. Protectorate agent Ya-six is trapped and badly injured in the Ultris mine and asks for help, saying the void lord Arconus has been feeding on the creatures here. Withered corpses, fleshfiends and voidwraiths roam the grounds.

You are in Celestial Ridge, a Netherstorm ridge where the strange nether dragons are studied. Tyri, a blue dragon of the brood of Malygos, and her companion Jorad Mace watch the dragons and their eggs, and Tyri is concerned that outsiders will exploit them. A shrouded figure also observes from a projection. Ethereum jailors and craghide basilisks prowl the ridge.

You are in The Stormspire, a Netherstorm center where the Consortium trades. The innkeeper Eyonix offers rest for a modest fee, and Ghabar, the head Eco-Dome engineer, worries over unexplained generator failures. Zuben Elgenubi is building a farahlite market, and an image of Nexus-Prince Haramad speaks to visitors through an imaging device. Talbuk sires are a danger on the grounds.
You are in Forge Base: Oblivion, a forge base in Netherstorm. Gan'arg mekgineers, terrorguard protectors and Legion fel cannons make it dangerous, and a dormant fel reaver sits among them.
You are in Forge Base: Gehenna, a forge base in Netherstorm. Cyber-rage forgelords, wrathbringers and wrath priestesses make it dangerous, and Legion fel cannons are among them.

You are in Ruins of Farahlon, a ruined site in Netherstorm overrun by demons. Culuthas holds them with hounds and eyes of Culuthas, and the excavator Zephyrion cannot begin work while demonic occupation continues.
You are in Socrethar's Seat, a place in Netherstorm where wrath lords and hatecryers gather. Socrethar himself is among them.
You are in Sunfury Hold, a Netherstorm hold of sunfury archers, flamekeepers and researchers, with nether beasts roaming its halls. Spellreaver Marathelle is among them.
You are in Netherstone, a landmark in Netherstorm where newly exposed formations yield farahlite. Farahlon breakers and Cragskaar, patriarch of the Farahlon giants, make the ground dangerous.

You are in Midrealm Post, a Consortium post in Netherstorm. Dealer Dunar sells goods, and Gahruj, the Consortium representative, is pressing the blood elves of Manaforge Duro for unpaid surveying equipment. Mama Wheeler, a B.O.O.M. mech tech, wants fel reaver parts gathered from the Scrap Field, now overrun by the Burning Legion, and ripfang lynxes roam nearby.

You are in Tuluman's Landing, a trading post in Netherstorm beside the bridge to Manaforge Ara. Wind Trader Tuluman sells weapons here, and the post offers repairs as well. Nether-Stalker Oazul of the Consortium condemns the blood elves' manaforge work, and Kaylaan, a combatant serving Orelis, grows weary of orders against the naaru's enemies.

You are in Protectorate Watch Post, an outpost of the ethereal Protectorate in Netherstorm. Commander Ameer leads here and has little patience for outsiders, while Dealer Hazzin supplies travelers bound for Manaforge Ultris. Researcher Navuud warns that void waste around Ultris can congeal into a void horror. Professor Dabiri focuses on stopping Dimensius.

You are in Gyro-Plank Bridge, a span in Netherstorm where B.O.O.M. netherologist Coppernickels studies the nether away from the town. His second-hand equipment keeps failing, and he fears the nearby blood elves think he is spying.

You are in The Proving Grounds, a B.O.O.M. testing site in Netherstorm where experimentalist Doctor Vomisa, Ph.T. builds and tests inventions for the defense of Area 52. His Scrap Reaver X6000, a mechanical combatant, is put through its trials here.

You are in Eco-Dome Farfield, one of the Eco-Domes in Netherstorm, where Consortium technician Tashar tests a portable generator repair kit designed by Ghabar. Scythetooth raptors and a tyrantus roam the grounds and threaten the test, and Tashar worries about the failing dome.

You are in Eco-Dome Skyperch, one of the Eco-Domes in Netherstorm. Talbuk sires roam here, and Farahlon lashers, dangerous living plants, are found here too. Talbuk does can call a male to their side.

You are in Eco-Dome Sutheron, an Eco-Dome in Netherstorm. Talbuk sires and a markaru threaten the grounds, and Farahlon lashers, dangerous living plants, grow here as well. Arcane vortices are met here too.
You are in Eco-Dome Midrealm, an Eco-Dome in Netherstorm where shimmerwing moths live. Ripfang lynxes and barbscale crocolisks prowl the dome, and mana snappers lurk there too.

You are in Ethereum Staging Grounds, an Ethereum base in Netherstorm directly south of Protectorate Watch Post. Ethereum overlords, assassins, archons and shocktroopers fight here, and Nexus-King Salhadaar is shielded by force fields from three conduits. Captain Tyralius of the Protectorate is believed held in a cell.

You are in Chapel Yard, a yard of Kirin'Var Village in Netherstorm. Tormented souls and tormented citizens haunt the yard, and Naberius is among the spirits that trouble it. Thadell's prize cow, Bessy, is known for her cowbell.

You are in Access Shaft Zeon, a Protectorate post in Netherstorm on the south side of Manaforge Ultris. Agent Araxes stays outside the shaft, and withered corpses and fleshfiends haunt the place, with Ever-Core the Punisher the most notable danger.
You are in Arklonis Ridge, a ridge in Netherstorm. Farahlon giants and farahlon crumblers roam it, along with shaleskin flayers, and arcane vortices are met here too.

You are in Town Square, in the ruins of Kirin'Var Village in Netherstorm. Blood elves destroyed the Kirin Tor village, and its dead mages linger as spirits. Custodian Dieworth, an undead keeper, mourns them here, while Severed Spirits and Severed Defenders wander the square. Repairs and a vendor are on hand.
You are in Wizard Row in Netherstorm. Mana Seekers and Mageslayers haunt its ruins. Ravenous mana elementals are drawn here and keep wrecking what is left.

You are in Trelleum Mine, a mine in Netherstorm, held by neither the Alliance nor the Horde. Its former foreman, Foreman Sundown, was demoted and now claims the blood elves' pilgrimage to Outland was a pretext Kael'thas used to build his forces here, urging his kin to leave as the Burning Legion advances. Sunfury nethermancers, blood knights and Gan'arg warp-tinkers haunt the workings.
